claims.text: Conventional ceria-based automotive exhaust catalyst supports are typically loaded with PGM nanoparticles.
Surface-confined atomic high-entropy oxide layers can be fabricated on ceria nanocrystals.
The proposed HEO layer can be composed of multiple first-row transition metals such as Cu, Co, Fe, Ni, and Mn.
The surface-confined HEO layer forms an interface with the ceria substrate.
Transition-metal–oxygen bonds at the HEO–ceria interface have increased covalent character.
Increased interfacial covalency promotes the formation of surface oxygen vacancies.
The HEO layer stabilizes surface oxygen vacancies.
Surface oxygen vacancies enable efficient oxygen activation and replenishment.
Oxygen activation and replenishment at the HEO–ceria interface enhance oxidation catalysis.
The interfacial oxygen-vacancy mechanism will enhance catalytic activity under simulated automotive exhaust conditions.
The HEO coating will improve catalyst durability during repeated high-temperature redox, thermal, and chemical cycling.
The improved reactivity will permit reduced PGM loading.
HEO-coated catalysts will have lower light-off temperatures than conventional PGM-loaded ceria catalysts.
HEO-coated catalysts will retain activity better during long-term thermal cycling than conventional catalysts.
HEO-coated catalysts with 30–50% less PGM will provide similar or enhanced conversion relative to conventional catalysts with standard PGM loading.
A large size mismatch between first-row transition metals and cerium can limit stabilization of ceria-based mixed oxides or compromise the desired interface.
The benefit may disappear at operating temperatures outside the regime in which oxygen vacancies are activated.
Long-term chemical compatibility and mechanical integrity of the HEO layer in real-world exhaust cycling have not been fully demonstrated.
